function.name: BitmapImpl_AcquireLock
function.description: This function acquires a lock on a BitmapImpl object. If the 'write' parameter is true, it tries to set the lock to -1. If the 'write' parameter is false, it enters a loop where it tries to increment the lock value until it succeeds.

parameters.name: This
parameters.description: The BitmapImpl object on which to acquire the lock.

parameters.name: write
parameters.description: A flag indicating whether to write to the object. If true, the function tries to set the lock to -1. If false, the function tries to increment the lock value.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the lock was successfully acquired. Returns TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: BitmapImpl_ReleaseLock
function.description: This function releases a lock on a BitmapImpl object by decrementing the lock value until it can be successfully updated to a new value.

parameters.name: This
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the BitmapImpl object whose lock is to be released.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return any value

function.name: BitmapLockImpl_QueryInterface
function.description: This function is used to query the interface of a Bitmap Lock object. It checks if the provided interface identifier (IID) matches the IUnknown interface or the IWICBitmapLock interface. If it does, it assigns the address of the IWICBitmapLock interface to the provided void pointer. If it doesn't, it sets the void pointer to NULL and returns an error.

parameters.name: iface
parameters.description: Pointer to the Bitmap Lock object.

parameters.name: iid
parameters.description: Interface identifier to be checked against.

parameters.name: ppv
parameters.description: Pointer to a void pointer where the address of the interface will be stored if the IID matches.

function.return_type: HRESULT, represents the status of the operation. It returns S_OK if the operation is successful, E_INVALIDARG if the ppv parameter is NULL, and E_NOINTERFACE if the provided IID does not match any known interfaces.
